card.name: Indingala
card.tagline: Northern Malawi warrior dance of the Nyakyusa and Ngonde
card.profile: Indingala is a traditional dance of the Nyakyusa and Ngonde peoples of Karonga and Chitipa districts in northern Malawi (and across the border in Tanzania, their earlier homeland) (SDNP Malawi). It originated as a warrior dance: 'indingala' was a special drum used to signal a chief's death, dangerous animals or an enemy attack, summoning armed men to the scene (SDNP Malawi). Today it is a peaceful, highly expressive dance for emotional release, with little singing and music supplied by three drums and whistles; dancers throw their bodies in different directions while coordinating arm and leg movements (SDNP Malawi).
card.insight: Indingala is the parent dance from which the joyous school dance Mwinoghe was modified between 1953 and 1955 (UNESCO; SDNP Malawi).
